paragraphs: Some guy majestically writes to me in DMs that he found reading about vibe-coding more interesting than about games, and if I want to keep him as a subscriber I'd better come to my senses, or he's almost made the decision to unsubscribe.
… man, first of all go … yourself, and take your imaginary buddies with you.

Second.. Can there really be stronger content about vibe-coding than from a guy who four months ago was asking people what a firewall on Hetzner is, and who built an entire platform of networked games, some of which weren't even networked (Arcomage). Shoved … Counter-Strike and Quake into the browser and … it to a one-click launch with alerts and achievements etc.?
Or what is vibe-coding content supposed to be about? =)))))))
… monkey you are.
Make Telegram great again …!
There must be people here subscribed to a mass of channels. Suggest mechanics the neighbors are vibe-coding; I have no time to look there, but I have time to build:)

Over today play.mountkendall.com got … by hundreds of commits, and there's still tomorrow, the day after and the remaining days:) Your reports in the chat are priceless. I'll do everything needed to make it …:**

My little system is developing too, but you can't do more than X there, and I put all free tokens into developing the community and the bicep of the skill of making things. I really want to keep going in the right direction)
By morning check out the guilds tab; a lot will change there)
However, at least it doesn't … like … SOL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
But how to orchestrate it now isn't particularly clear.

Everything is heading toward this (and you can really feel it at your fingertips): $1,000 of models is work on ONE task, with a thinker attached for how to correctly spend on it so as to work continuously.

But people who remember my content also remember that we talked about this even before I learned to vibe-code… Sam Altman and his … talked about this back in 2023. That, like, an agent that performs your task (a TASK) for you 24/7 will cost about 2,500 a month.
Meaning that even with all these squeezes of the last ±1.5 months we most likely haven't even come close to sniffing the real cost of vibe-coding in the near future.
I'll be laughing really hard if in the end they also put us before a choice (and they will).

A tasty plan at 2,500 will simply appear at every vendor. At the Chinese ones, with every payment you'll be able to spin 100 roulettes that give out Temu prizes like funny blue Labubus. At the Americans there'll be no roulettes, but there'll be blue ones.

At the Europeans, those lucky ones who manage to earn something on vibe-coding will spend the dough in museums, and secretly touch blue objects before bed, and also buy blueberries at the supermarket, because on vacation you can afford damn extravagance!!!
But actually, before bed, I'll … you such a life-affirming thing, which continuously brings me back to life and amuses me. Not only in vibe-coding, but in general.
Here in the screenshot you see something that didn't exist in nature…. three calendar weeks ago.
Since then vibe-coding has changed beyond recognition. Those got cheaper, these got more expensive, everyone hacked everyone, men got pregnant, girls formed cartels.
3 weeks.
But even these 3 weeks can be divided into several segments.
And I've been vibe-coding, let's say, seriously since December.
So … I can cut such segments every few days, I swear.

Just remember that everything you see today is absolutely irrelevant. You and I are watching a movie, and guys like me are those … dudes who sometimes toss comments at the whole theater and throw popcorn at pretty girls. Then get … from their boyfriends.
Call up their bros and lay the boyfriends out.
But the boyfriends turned out to be a lieutenant colonel's kids, so in the end everyone simply gets beaten all around.
If I'd become mayor of Novosibirsk, I'd have … enough money for a one-way ticket somewhere the … out of this … country =)))
Fortunately you didn't have to become mayor for that.
In short, boys and girls — photograph the moments; we are those very 0.01% of the living who are touching all this with our hands at all and watching the birth happen.
And it won't even give us anything specific in the long-run sense. In a year it'll simply do everything itself without us. “Vibe-coding skills” is a sad joke.
But nevertheless each of us will take something useful out of this whole story. Something that will be very hard to explain, but it'll be tangible, and it'll unite.
Like push-button phones, pagers, cassettes and floppies, squealing modems, and other … from the backwoods of history.
Remember how long all these elements existed in your life, each of them? The same 3–4 years actually;)))))))
We're growing up and life flies ever faster, as if the old folks hadn't told us about this all through childhood.
I can't wait to see what happens next, when this … hatches, what we'll be spamming the Internets with then and annoying our significant others with, and plunging friends into bewilderment))
Okay, so in short, guys, as you know, I've been practicing necrophilia, screwing my brain long since atrophied by vibe-coding, as historians say, “since time immemorial.”

Today I was boasting to myself about a truly grandiose breakthrough: I achieved a quality of market scan higher than anything I've ever done with my own hands. Even for $100k I couldn't have spent enough time and cognitive effort to produce such quality of such breadth in a year of work — which the market scan is now able to produce entirely without my participation, without me pressing a single button or even being aware it's happening.
This is exactly what I need in order to release my self-serve SLSBMB AI in the near future, which I've been striving toward so furiously these last few months.
To say that I repeatedly ran tests on different models to understand which models the market scan works best on is to say nothing. I think I've burned tens of billions of tokens on these experiments.
At the peak the madness reached the point where one market scan FOR ONE PRODUCT used ~290–500 SEQUENTIAL SESSIONS …. A record run like that easily took 2.5 days.

In the end I managed to refine the paperwork the market scan and all the runs live on such that 4 sequential sessions are enough: Research (up to 50 minutes), Writer (up to 50 minutes), Market Arms (what the types of companies and job titles we'll be writing to are called, up to 50 minutes), and the Judge (checks everything done by the 3 previous sessions against a gigantic checklist, and can send individual pieces back for rework).
I've already said I've been building this particular system for several months, and it has drunk all my blood, as well as my semen, the fluid of my tear glands, and my prostate secretions.
I do this around the clock, and it's … me quite a bit.
But I don't give up.

And so today I got colossal results, and what remained was, for the … umpteenth time, to run the experiment not on the specific set of models I believe in but on different models, and compare each segment with the others, to understand which of the runners to run on which model for maximum combinatorial efficiency.
Essentially I just had to run the whole market scan (all 4 of its sessions) on each of the models, several times, and get averages that could be considered representative.
Again, since I'm doing this not for the first or third dozen times, I think the result is genuinely representative, and not a case of “someone did something and called it a benchmark.”
I wouldn't … show you a random one after such torments, because I'll have to answer for it later when I start selling this solution to some of you for … cash;))))))

The next message will bring the anonymized but sufficient-to-understand-the-difference-between-models-in-the-creative-field result of this gigantic test, which took the whole of today. You'll see averages over a string of repeated re-runs of the most resonant models.

The only thing I won't be able to show you is Fable 5 and Opus 5, since they're no longer in my roster, but I don't grieve for them at all, since I already know on the basis of DOZENS of experiments how they'd have performed. Fable would have performed worse than Opus. Fable is generally quite mediocre in the current field on questions of creative depth in texts and the meanings around a unit of text quality. Opus is much better; it's neck and neck … with GPT 5.5 xhigh, since these are essentially the models that compete with each other in the niche. However GPT 5.5 Xhigh is more stable. In general the stability of GPT 5.5 Xhigh is astonishing. This model is far from as creative as QWEN3.8MAX in text, but QWEN3.8MAX can somehow …, including simply not answering … an API request, whereas GPT 5.5 xhigh is the most stable model in nature. It will deliver its 7/10 in texts so stably that even if you run it 1,000 times on 1,000 texts each time, the quality will be exactly what you expect. That's not great for those who aren't ready to write damn treatises of quality methodology for the runner to lean on, but it's … how good for people like me =)

In the end, specifically for Writing, I use QWEN3.8MAX with fallback to GPT 5.5 xhigh, where the fallback is tricky — they'll both always write content, it's just that the judge has to choose between the two, and in 30% of cases it chooses 5.5 xhigh, which is an incredibly cool result for a model that's many months old.

And the leader on the other criteria I think you'll easily see. Many think Fable is Sol's competitor, but in research tasks Fable shows numbers 5 OR MORE TIMES lower than Sol. On these creative tasks of mine that's simply a fact. Fable is next to Kimi. Sol Max is somewhere in outer space.

If only this … could code without going insane, it'd be priceless. On research and writing tasks Sol Max amazingly doesn't go insane. It really finishes all the work itself and wraps up in 50 minutes (versus 17 minutes for 5.5 xhigh). On coding tasks it basically never wraps up; at least I never once waited it out, simply force-terminating it in the 15th to 50th hour of work.
Honestly, I don't fully understand why so few people play Q3 and CS 1.6:)
I understand chess — not for everyone. The other little games like various checkers, I never thought anyone would play at all, I made them simply out of some inexplicable impulse.
But Quake 3 and Counter-Strike 1.6… Here it's kind of impossible to imagine that someone who has a soul at all and a normal mouse wouldn't want to duke it out with buddies.
However, about ten people out of THOUSANDS play.

And as far as I understand, people play only among the existing chat members. Nobody even invited buddies unrelated to the chat to a server available in one click in the browser, for which you need to do nothing but a few clicks.
It turns out Quake 3 and CS 1.6 are an absolutely obsolete game in our human cohort. Or people simply haven't figured out that you can invite buddies to play this way?
Or something else? Someone explain it to me plz)
I'm not exactly complaining, it doesn't bring me money, I just sincerely don't understand where the miscalculation is here?
Do people these days not play on the computer at all? Or do they play on the PlayStation? Or are shooters now too stressful and everyone's grinding some platformers?
Think about this number: in the whole time the server has been running, fewer than 50 people have played Q3 and CS 1.6) Most of them came in once purely to gawk and never came back.
So CS 1.6 and Q3 are less interesting than CHESS.
… the intellectual elite has gathered here; I should vibe-code a hadron collider for you)
Hi chat, recently we were riffing about visualizing a project — what's happening in it right now and what it looks like from a bird's-eye view in general.
If this is still relevant to anyone besides 3 people here — take it, poke it, look with your eyes, touch with your hands, mom definitely won't scold you: https://github.com/m0ast-git/repo-canvas

What it is: a tool that, after installation, requires your agent to build a full map of the project and spread it onto a canvas. Then it picks up the cheapest model from your codex/claude/kimi subscription and sets it as an observer that triggers on agents' actions in your repo. So this observer first sees “something's happening,” goes to look at “what's happening,” describes it properly and places it on the canvas as an active element with its description.

The agent's work card at the same time contains a direct local link to the session currently puffing away at the task — if it doesn't suit you or you realize something's going wrong, then double-click, jump into the session, “stop” button.

Besides these wonderful functions, the canvas will help revive in your head the full map of the project, re-study all the connections between modules and understand how … everything is as of “here and now.”
